title: long-context-kvstutter-lab-journal
content:
This is a running scratchpad for the long-context kv-stutter issue (intermittent token drop / garbled output) that shows up in production when sequence length crosses certain boundaries (~4kish tokens). Goal: gather repro steps, commands I ran, raw error snippets, micro-benchmarks, and hypotheses to hand off to kernel/serving owners.

Summary of observed behavior
- Symptom: model output abruptly repeats a short prefix or emits garbled tokens after ~L tokens. Not consistent but correlated with request seq_len distribution (many long prefixes + short churn).
- Affects: 13B and 30B variants (float16 & int8 quantized), host and dedicated pools. More frequent when batch contains mixed seqlen (one long request + N short).
- Timing: showed up after recent kernel selection change (auto-fuse heuristics landed on main 2026-01-18).

Quick reproduction (local container)
- Env: docker image reg.redwood/runtime-debug:kvstutter-2026-02, CUDA 12.3, cuDNN 9.1, pytorch-ish runtime shim.
- Command (approx):
  # run a microserver with kv emulation
  ./start_inference_server --model rwinf-13b-q4_0 --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 --kv-mode persistent --attn-kernel auto 

- Repro script (python snippet):
  import requests
  def gen(prefix, extra):
      body = {"prompt": prefix + extra, "max_tokens": 128}
      r = requests.post('http://127.0.0.1:8080/generate', json=body, timeout=30)
      return r.text

  long_prefix = ' '.join(['token']*3800)  # ~3800 tokens
  short = ' hello'
  print(gen(long_prefix, ''))
  print(gen('', short))  # mix long then short in same batch

Observed raw snippets
- Example output where issue occurs (truncated):
  >>> ... token token token token 
  <garbled> \x80\x9f\x00\x01 repeat: token token token token token
  (then model stalls emiting the same 12-token prefix)

- Server logs near time of event:
  [2026-02-25 14:33:12.442] warn: kv-layer: found overlapping slot window: start=4096 end=8192 candidate_start=0
  [2026-02-25 14:33:12.443] debug: attn-kernel: selected=FUSED_ATTN_TILE32 fallback=CAUSAL_REF
  [2026-02-25 14:33:12.444] error: kv-commit: mismatch expected-offset=4096 observed-offset=0

Commands I tried to probe offsets
- Dumped KV headers immediately after request: ./kv_dump --target localhost:8080 --range 0-8192 > kvhdr.log- Result: header entries show two sessions with offsets 0 and 4096 for same request-id (possible aliasing)
- Forced single-session mode: ./start_inference_server --session-mode single -> failure reduced but not eliminated
- Re-ran with ATTN_KERNEL=CAUSAL_REF enforced -> issue disappears in 7/8 runs, but latency regresses x1.6
- Re-ran with ATTN_KERNEL=FUSED_HYBRID -> issue persists about 50% of runs

Microbench numbers (median over 10 runs)
- auto kernel: latency 112ms, p95 280ms, kv-fail rate ~18%
- causal_ref: latency 176ms, p95 320ms, kv-fail rate ~2%
- fused_tile32: latency 98ms, p95 260ms, kv-fail rate ~22%

Hypotheses (ordered by my confidence)
1) KV slot aliasing when sequence boundary aligns with tile boundary: some kernel writes KV to a transient buffer then copies back with wrong base index when request seqlen % tile_size == 0. (Evidence: logs show expected-offset=4096 observed-offset=0)
2) Race between KV commit and attention kernel completion when batching mixes long + short - merged completion callback doesn't correctly synchronize for fused kernels. (Evidence: only reproduces on fused kernels; causal_ref avoids it)
3) Off-by-one in prefix length normalization in the serving layer: length quantization for compression/packing produces a 1-token shift if length divisible by 32. (Weak)
4) Memory reclamation path frees the backing buffer before downstream IO completes when quantized kernels use staging buffers. (Possible, but would likely manifest as segfaults; we see garbled bytes instead)

Things to test next (actionable)
- Add a deterministic micro-repro harness that directly calls kernel A and then reads the KV buffer with memory fence to check for write-after-free. I sketched a reproducer in repo at linked PR.
- Add additional instrumentation at kv-commit to log callstack + kernel id when offsets mismatch. Quick patch: increment a per-request counter at kernel entry/exit and assert commit counter >= kernel counter.
- Try forcing single-kernel-path for mixed batches and measure effect (already tried single-session but need single-kernel).
- Run with ASAN on CPU fallback to catch heap corruption (slow but high signal).
- Capture GPU traces (Nsight) for a failing run to see scheduling of kernels and memcpy operations.

Notes on kernel selection heuristics (from reading runtime code)
- attn-kernel selection uses heuristic: if seqlen_avg >= 1024 and dtype==f16 => FUSED_TILE32 preferred; else CAUSAL_REF. There is a second pass that considers batch variance: if var>0.2 then prefer hybrid. Suspect the "hybrid" path triggers codegen path that uses a temporary KV staging buffer per warp.
- env override ATTN_KERNEL forces mapping but there are also per-model tunables stored in model-config.json. Ensure both are consistent.

Patches/PR ideas
- Short-term: enforce a write barrier before kv-commit for fused kernels: gpuStreamSynchronize(stream) or explicit event records after kernel then before device->host copy. Pros: quick mitigation. Cons: adds latency and we must measure p95 impact.
- Mid-term: fix index arithmetic in staging-to-global copy to use 64-bit offsets and validate range. Add unit tests around tile-aligned sizes and mixed seqlen batches.

Notes from offline chat with Diego
- Diego: "I saw a similar report in SERV-2314; there we also had a stale request-id reuse causing KV collision. Worth checking session-id assignment across workers."
- Hannah: "If forcing causal removes issue, we should add sampling fallback to causal per 1/1000 requests when kernel==fused AND seqlen>threshold."

Immediate todo (my checklist)
- [ ] Add assert + logging to kv-commit for offset sanity checks (low-risk).
- [ ] Reproduce with deterministic seed and capture GPU timeline (Nsight).
- [ ] Try single-kernel fallback policy in a canary pool for a day.
- [ ] Add unit test for tile boundary sizes (32, 64, 128) with mixed seqlen batches.
- [ ] Draft a short runbook for SRE on how to detect when the issue spikes (log patterns / kv offsets).

Random logs / snippets kept for posterity
- gdb backtrace (from a run that crashed):
  #0  0x00007f9a5b2c in memcpy_from_device (dst=0x7f000, src=0x8f000, n=16384)
  #1  0x00007f9a6c3d in kv_staging_copy
  #2  0x000055bb7a12 in commit_kv_entries

- quick grep results:
  $ git grep "staging_buffer" -n runtime || true
  runtime/kv_manager.cc:211: // allocate staging_buffer when use_staging && tile_aligned
  runtime/kv_manager.cc:234: staging_copy(device_ptr, global_base + offset)

Closing notes
- This doc is a messy scratchpad; aim to convert to a clean postmortem or PR description once repro is nailed.
- If you pick this up: start with the kv-commit assert patch (low-risk) and collect trigger logs for a failing run to attach to the PR.

Last checked: 2026-03-10 by Aisha
